name: Web probe
description: Probe one business's website the way an AI that reads only the site would, and answer fixed questions about it as JSON: name, trade, services, prices, area served, contact details, hours, next step for a customer, trust signals, structured data, inconsistencies, a clarity score, a short summary, and what the site leaves out. The fetch step runs `~/.darkmux/scripts/web-probe-fetch.sh` (curl, plus textutil on macOS) on this machine and reads the home page and up to four linked pages on the same site; no model touches the network. The probe task hands that text to the tool-less web-probe role, whose answer is held to its JSON schema, then prints it, writes it to `out` when given, and makes it the run's close payload.

inputs.name: url
inputs.description: The site to probe: `https://example.com/`, or a bare `example.com` (read as https).

inputs.name: out
inputs.description: A file to write the JSON answer to. Absent, the answer is only printed and kept as the run's close payload.

inputs.name: dry_run
inputs.description: The generic `mission launch --dry-run` flag, injected by the CLI layer, never set by hand.

phases.description: Fetch the site's home page and its linked pricing, services, contact and about pages on this machine.
The web-probe role answers the fixed questions; the second step delivers the answer.

config.message: A business's website is above, as one or more `<web-page>` blocks. Answer the questions in your instructions about this business, using only what those pages say, as one JSON object.
